title: Fix Hanging Test In Mathematical CAS Crate
description: cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast hung on the mathematical_cas crate (mathematical/cas/rs) test binary, consuming 110+ minutes CPU with no completion, blocking the full workspace test run. git diff --stat on mathematical/cas/rs/lib.rs shows no changes from any recent session, so this is a pre-existing bug, not concurrent-edit fallout. Plan: enumerate mathematical_cas lib tests, run each individually under a timeout to isolate the hanging one, inspect for infinite loop / unbounded recursion / exponential blowup (likely in CAS simplification or factoring code), fix the root cause (bound depth/iterations or fix termination condition), and verify the full crate test suite completes in reasonable time.
summary:
Root-caused and fixed the `cargo test --workspace` hang in `mathematical_cas`. Isolated each of the 138 lib tests individually (perl `alarm`-based timeout, since macOS lacks `timeout(1)`) and found 6 tests genuinely hanging, all going through real-root isolation / integer factorization (rootof, solve, ode, integrate). Sampled the hung process (macOS `sample`) and traced the hang to two independent root-cause bugs, both fixed:

1. `ModInt::neg()` in mathematical/number/rs/lib.rs didn't actually negate "unbound" (modulus-agnostic) values produced by `Ring::zero()/one()` — `neg(1)` returned `1` unchanged. This silently turned `PolyU::sub` into `PolyU::add` whenever one operand was `PolyU::one()`/`PolyU::zero()`, corrupting the Cantor-Zassenhaus equal-degree-factorization loop (used by integer polynomial factorization) so it looped effectively forever instead of converging in O(1) expected iterations. Fixed by giving unbound `ModInt` values a proper signed (two's-complement bit-pattern) representation: `neg()` now wraps correctly, and `unify()` reduces an unbound operand into the target modulus via signed `rem_euclid` instead of passing the raw bit pattern through. Also fixed the matching `from_i64` sign-drop and made the both-unbound `add`/`mul` paths use wrapping arithmetic instead of panicking-on-overflow raw `+`/`*`.

2. `pseudo_div_rem` in mathematical/polynomial/rs/lib.rs scaled the remainder by the divisor's leading coefficient *before* reading off the term used to cancel the leading term, instead of after. This only produced a correct pseudo-division step when the divisor happened to be monic; for any non-monic divisor (e.g. `5x^4-1`, the derivative of `x^5-x-1`) the leading term never actually canceled, growing exponentially every iteration — a second, independent infinite loop hit by Sturm-sequence construction for `solve_high_degree_gives_rootof`.

Unblocking these hangs also surfaced two smaller, directly-related bugs in mathematical/cas/rs/lib.rs's own logic for the same 6 tests (previously unreachable because the process never terminated): `root_of_to_f64` returned the raw isolating interval's midpoint without ever refining it, giving ~1.5 instead of √2; fixed by refining to a small width first. `integrate_partial_fraction_term` only matched `Kind::Mul` terms, missing the case where a partial-fraction term with unit numerator canonicalizes to a bare `Kind::Pow` (e.g. `(x^2+1)^-1`), causing `integrate(1/(x^2+1))` to return `None`; fixed by handling both shapes.

Verified: `cargo test -p mathematical_cas --lib` now completes in 0.02s (was: 110+ min hang, never completing). All 6 originally-hanging tests now pass. Also ran `mathematical_polynomial`'s own suite (never run before touching this code) and confirmed via careful before/after isolation that none of the fixes caused regressions — every remaining failure (7 in mathematical_cas, 6 in mathematical_polynomial) reproduces identically on the fully unmodified baseline code, either as a pre-existing hang (now unmasked into a precision/logic failure) or a pre-existing direct failure. Flagged both clusters as separate follow-up tasks (spawn_task) since they're unrelated to the hang and span several independent subsystems (ODE solving, series closed-forms, limits, algebraic-number precision, polynomial interpolation, irreducibility testing).

Full workspace build (`cargo build --workspace --lib`) verified clean after the fix. No temp/debug instrumentation left in any lib.rs — all removed before finalizing.
